prompt: What did the second `pull.ts all` cost, with nothing changed on the server?

choices.text: The device skipped it, having pulled moments before
choices.why: pull.ts all always asks for everything.

choices.text: 28 bytes
choices.why: That is a delta pull with nothing new.

choices.text: The same 217,837 bytes as the first
choices.why: Right. The cost follows the data, not the change.

choices.text: Half, because the second response is compressed by the server
choices.why: Nothing here compresses; the bytes were identical.

prompt: Why can replacing the local copy with everything only run when the outbox is empty?

choices.text: It would throw away changes the server has not seen
choices.why: Right. Lesson 12 shows a full download that keeps them.

choices.text: SQLite cannot delete and insert in one transaction
choices.why: It can; pull.ts does both.

choices.text: The server refuses downloads while there are uploads
choices.why: The server knows nothing of the outbox.

choices.text: The cursor would be lost
choices.why: The cursor is not the problem; the device's own changes are.

choices.text: The time of the device's last sync
choices.why: That is the timestamp design the lesson replaces.

choices.text: The id of the last session the person opened on the device
choices.why: It is a position in the server's history, not on a screen.

choices.text: A count of rows on the device
choices.why: After the delete, the device had 5 rows and cursor 7.

choices.text: The last write it read
choices.why: Right, handed out by the server and given back to it.

prompt: How many bytes did a delta pull with nothing new receive in the lesson's run?
Why does `pull.ts` save the rows and the new cursor in one transaction?

choices.text: Transactions make the pull smaller
choices.why: Size is decided by the server's answer.

choices.text: A crash could skip them
choices.why: Right: a cursor saved without its rows skips them for ever, while rows without the cursor are merely fetched twice.

choices.text: The server requires it
choices.why: The server cannot see the device's transactions.

choices.text: To stop two drains at once
choices.why: That is lesson 8's lock, a different problem.

prompt: A developer notices the cursor is a number and makes the app send `cursor - 100` 'to be safe'. What does the lesson say?

choices.text: Fine: it only refetches a hundred rows
choices.why: It works here and breaks the day the server's cursor stops being a number.

choices.text: The device must store and return it, never compute with it
choices.why: Right. The cursor is opaque by contract.

choices.text: It is the overlap repair, and the lesson recommends it
choices.why: The overlap is for time windows, which have no server-made order.

choices.text: The server will answer 410
choices.why: 410 is for a cursor older than the history kept.

prompt: In `clocks.ts`, why did the timestamp query return nothing?

choices.text: Phone B's write failed
choices.why: The cursor query returned it, so it was written.

choices.text: The server sorts timestamps alphabetically, and that order is wrong for times
choices.why: ISO times sort correctly as text; the stamp itself was early.

choices.text: A asked too soon
choices.why: It asked at 10:10, after the write.

choices.text: B stamped it 09:55, before A's 10:00 bookmark
choices.why: Right. Written after, stamped before.

prompt: A back end offers only `updated_at`. Which repair does the lesson put first?

choices.text: Have the server write it on arrival
choices.why: Right. One clock, one machine's error.

choices.text: Ask the person to check their phone's clock before syncing
choices.why: A sync cannot depend on that.

choices.text: Overlap the window by a few minutes each time
choices.why: That is the second repair: it survives small skew.

choices.text: Use the phone's clock, but in UTC
choices.why: A slow clock is slow in every zone.

prompt: Which of these leave a phone's clock wrong, according to the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the person setting it by hand to cheat a game
choices.why: One of the lesson's cases.

choices.text: a week switched off
choices.why: It drifts.

choices.text: a tablet with the wrong zone
choices.why: One of the lesson's cases.

choices.text: using a cursor to sync
choices.why: A cursor never reads the phone's clock.

prompt: A cursor is decided in one place, the ___, in the order the writes arrived.
What is a tombstone in this lesson?

choices.text: A row the device forgot to send
choices.why: That is a pending row.

choices.text: An operation the server refused
choices.why: That is lesson 8's dead operation.

choices.text: A deleted row kept as a numbered write
choices.why: Right, so a delta can carry the delete.

choices.text: A backup of a session kept in case the person wants it back later
choices.why: It records the delete; it is not there to undo it.

prompt: Without tombstones, what happens to s3 on a device that pulled it before it was deleted elsewhere?

choices.text: It stays
choices.why: Right, and a later send brings it back to life. Its 20 minutes stay in the week, too.

choices.text: The server sends a push to remove it
choices.why: Nothing here pushes.

choices.text: It disappears at the next delta pull
choices.why: No question can return a row that is gone.

choices.text: The device crashes on the next pull
choices.why: Nothing fails, which is the problem.

prompt: After the delete of s3, how many bytes did the device's delta pull receive?
Why can a server not keep tombstones only until every device has pulled past them?

choices.text: Tombstones are too large to keep
choices.why: Each is one row; the question is how long.

choices.text: Devices refuse old tombstones
choices.why: pull.ts applies any it receives.

choices.text: It cannot know about a phone in a drawer
choices.why: Right, so it keeps a fixed window and lesson 12 handles the rest.

choices.text: SQLite caps a table at a million rows
choices.why: It does not, and that is not the reason.

items: the device pulls the six sessions, cursor 6

the cursor pull receives the tombstone and leaves 5 sessions

prompt: A tablet that last synced 120 days ago comes back, and the server keeps tombstones for 90 days. What can a delta pull not tell it?

choices.text: Which sessions were created since
choices.why: Live rows are still in the history.

choices.text: The deletes older than 90 days
choices.why: Right. Their tombstones are gone, so it needs a full resync.

choices.text: Its own cursor, which the server erased along with the tombstones
choices.why: The cursor is on the tablet.

choices.text: Nothing: deltas work after any absence
choices.why: They work back to the oldest history kept, no further.

prompt: Two phones of the same person sync a week apart against the same server. What does the server keep per phone?

choices.text: Each phone's cursor
choices.why: The cursor lives on the phone and is sent back.

choices.text: A copy of the rows each phone has
choices.why: It keeps one history for both.

choices.text: The time each phone last synced
choices.why: Time is not what the server orders by.

choices.text: Nothing per phone; one history for both
choices.why: Right. Each phone keeps its own place in it.
